::: {#thm-holm-fwer}
#### Holm's procedure controls the FWER

If all p-values of true null hypotheses are valid (@def-valid-p-value),
[Holm's procedure](#def-holm) at level $\siglevel$ satisfies

$$\text{FWER} \le \siglevel,$$

whatever the dependence between the p-values.
:::

::: proof

If $m_0 = 0$ there is no true null hypothesis to reject, so $V = 0$ and $\text{FWER} = 0$.
If $m_0 \ge 1$, the event $V \ge 1$ means Holm's procedure rejects a true null hypothesis,
so by @sol-holm-threshold it is contained in the event $\min_{j \in \truenulls} p_j \le \siglevel / m_0$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{FWER}
&= \Prf{V \ge 1}
&& \text{(definition of the FWER)}\\
&\le \Prf{\min_{j \in \truenulls} p_j \le \frac{\siglevel}{m_0}}
&& \text{(the event $V \ge 1$ lies inside this event)}\\
&= \Prf{\bigcup_{j \in \truenulls} \set{p_j \le \frac{\siglevel}{m_0}}}
&& \text{(the minimum is at most a bound exactly when some term is)}\\
&\le \sum_{j \in \truenulls} \Prf{p_j \le \frac{\siglevel}{m_0}}
&& \text{(union bound)}\\
&\le \sum_{j \in \truenulls} \frac{\siglevel}{m_0}
&& \text{(each $p_j$ is valid, with $u = \siglevel / m_0$)}\\
&= m_0 \cdot \frac{\siglevel}{m_0}
&& \text{(a sum of $m_0$ equal terms)}\\
&= \siglevel
&& \text{($m_0 \cdot \frac{1}{m_0} = 1$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The union bound is @thm-union-bound and validity is @def-valid-p-value.
As for the Bonferroni correction, no assumption about dependence is needed.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#exm-holm-fwer}
#### FWER of Holm's procedure in the simulated family

Repeating the simulation of @exm-rejection-counts 2000 times with Holm's procedure:

```{r}
#| label: fwer-holm
#| code-fold: false
set.seed(575)
sim_counts$holm <- run_simulation(function(p) holm_reject(p, 0.05))
summarize_counts(sim_counts$holm)
```

The estimated FWER, `r round(summarize_counts(sim_counts$holm)[["FWER"]], 3)`,
is below $\siglevel = 0.05$, up to simulation error.
Holm's power is `r round(summarize_counts(sim_counts$holm)[["power"]], 3)`,
against `r round(summarize_counts(sim_counts$bonferroni)[["power"]], 3)` for the Bonferroni correction:
Holm's procedure can only reject more, but here the extra rejections are rare.
:::
